newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN LEADS EAST PLAYERS IN ALL-STAR VOTING.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN LEADS EAST PLAYERS IN ALL-STAR VOTING.

text.p: Chicago Bulls star Michael Jordan is the leading vote-getter in the most recent returns of Eastern Conference fan balloting for the 1997 NBA All-Star Game.
Jordan, a 10-time All-Star, has 403,665 votes to move ahead of forward Grant Hill of the Detroit Pistons, who led all players in votes received the last two seasons.
Hill has 396,169 votes and is followed at the forward position by the Bulls tandem of Scottie Pippen (298,029) and Dennis Rodman (173,057).
Jordan is followed at guard by Penny Hardaway of Orlando (226,369) and Joe Dumars of Detroit (150,388). Hardaway was activated from the injured list this week and has played sparingly this season.

At centre, Patrick Ewing of the New York Knicks continues to lead fellow Georgetown big man Alonzo Mourning of the Miami Heat. Ewing has 285,531 votes, while Mourning has 209,029. A third former Georgetown star, Dikembe Mutombo of the Atlanta Hawks, is third with 77,924 votes.
The 46th annual NBA All-Star Game will be played at the Gund Arena in Cleveland on February 9. The top two vote-getters at both guard and forward will start, as will the centre with the most votes.
